clue.text: Fish hearts going bad

blocks.note: H is the abbreviation for hearts in card games
erring means straying from the right path

explanation.surface: A fish whose hearts have started to rot.
explanation.definitionFit: The herring is a common silvery food fish of the North Atlantic.

clue.text: Men in Hawaii area snubbed, as far as I can see?

definitions.text: as far as I can see?

indicators.note: in places the soldiers inside the state abbreviation
snubbed suggests a nose cut short, so the last letter of the area word goes

blocks.note: HI is the US postal code for Hawaii
OR, other ranks, means soldiers who are not officers
a zone is an area

explanation.surface: Men in a part of Hawaii ignored, so far as the speaker knows.
explanation.walkthrough: As far as I can see reads as a figure of speech; taken literally, it is the limit of a viewer's sight.
explanation.definitionFit: The horizon is the line where earth meets sky, the farthest point visible.

clue.text: What's taken up half of garden with tangled boundless growth?

definitions.text: What's taken up half of garden with tangled boundless growth?

indicators.note: half of a word keeps its first three of six letters
in a down entry, taken up means read upwards, from bottom to top
boundless means without bounds, so the first and last letters go
tangled means twisted together, so the remaining letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the first half of garden
growth with its outer letters removed

explanation.surface: A gardener's complaint about a weed overrunning half the plot.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: ragwort is a weed that spreads untidily over neglected ground. Wort is an old word for plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Ragwort is a yellow-flowered weed, poisonous to livestock, that colonises untended land.

clue.text: Start enjoying crossing river

indicators.note: crossing means spanning over, so the word for enjoying straddles the river abbreviation

blocks.note: to be into something is to enjoy it
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Setting off happily over a river.
explanation.definitionFit: An intro is an introduction, the opening part or start of something.

clue.text: Picture snapper framing boy on island

indicators.note: framing means surrounding like a frame, so the reptile goes round the boy and island

blocks.note: a gator, short for alligator, is a creature with snapping jaws
a lad is a boy
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A photographer framing a boy on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: Picture snapper suggests a photographer; picture is a film and snapper an alligator.
explanation.definitionFit: Gladiator is a 2000 Ridley Scott film, and picture is an informal word for a film.

clue.text: Trump (American Truss) throwing a fit

indicators.note: throwing something away discards it, so a letter is dropped from the truss

blocks.note: to cap something is to outdo or trump it
A is the abbreviation for American
a bale is a trussed bundle of hay
the letter thrown out of the bundle

explanation.surface: Donald Trump and Liz Truss, a former British prime minister, having a tantrum together.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitals make Trump and Truss look like the two politicians; here they are a verb and a bundle of hay, with the A removed from BALE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone fit for a task is competent enough, able to do it.

clue.text: Small volume published, say

blocks.note: CL is the abbreviation for centilitre, a small volume
a book that is out has been published

explanation.surface: A slim book released, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: Say looks like 'for example' but is a noun meaning influence, as in having a say.
explanation.definitionFit: Clout means influence or power, as does having a say in something.

clue.text: One who entices support around "Ed Stone"

indicators.note: around means encircling, so the support goes round the quoted words

blocks.note: a pier is a supporting pillar
taken as written
a pip is a fruit stone

explanation.surface: Backing for the Ed Stone, the slogan-carved slab Ed Miliband unveiled before the 2015 UK election.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotes make it look like one name; Ed and Stone are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pied Piper lured the rats and then the children out of Hamelin, so the name means a seductive leader.

clue.text: Cross old dog keeping cost up

indicators.note: keeping means holding on to, so the dog encloses the cost
in a down entry, up means read from bottom to top

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
a lab is a Labrador, a breed of dog
a fee is a cost or charge

explanation.surface: An elderly dog in a bad mood about rising expenses.
explanation.walkthrough: Cross looks like the adjective for angry, but it is the noun for a hybrid animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A beefalo is a hybrid bred from domestic cattle and the American bison.

clue.text: Unopened message about the setter's tip

indicators.note: unopened means without its opening, so the first letter of the message goes

blocks.note: a text is a phone message
re means about or concerning
the setter refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: A text left unread about some advice from the crossword's author.
explanation.walkthrough: Tip suggests advice, but it means the far end, the extreme.
explanation.definitionFit: The extreme of something is its furthest point or tip.

clue.text: Meet plenty of humour, e.g. at Taskmaster

indicators.note: plenty of something is a large share but not all, so the letters come from inside the run of words

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of humour, all of e.g. and at, and the start of Taskmaster

explanation.surface: A comedy show, Taskmaster, full of laughs.
explanation.walkthrough: Taskmaster is a British TV comedy panel game.
explanation.definitionFit: A regatta is a sporting meet of rowing or sailing races.

clue.text: Love poetry shunned by son at feast?

indicators.note: shunned means avoided, so the letter for son is kept out of the poetry

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O
verse is poetry
S is the abbreviation for son
taken as written

explanation.surface: A son who refuses to listen to love poems at a banquet.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that feasting need not mean too much; overindulging is one kind of feasting.
explanation.definitionFit: To feast is to eat lavishly, and overeating is eating more than is needed.

clue.text: Look after trimmed pelt import for animal expert

indicators.note: trimmed means cut short, so the last letter of the word for pelt goes
after places the look word following the trimmed verb

blocks.note: to pelt along is to rush or zoom
lo is an old word for look!
the import of a speech is its gist

explanation.surface: Caring for a cut-down animal skin brought in from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: Pelt looks like a skin, matching the animal theme, but it is the verb meaning to race.
explanation.definitionFit: A zoologist is a scientist who studies animals.

clue.text: Power behind trophy

blocks.note: P is the symbol for power
behind schedule means late

explanation.surface: The force that drives a team to a cup win.
explanation.definitionFit: A plate is a prize in racing or other sport, often a silver dish given to the winner.

clue.text: Mark and Matthew etc taking over church

indicators.note: taking in something means holding it, so the books enclose the cricket abbreviation

blocks.note: Matthew and the other gospels are in the New Testament, NT
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: Two gospel writers, Mark and Matthew, taking charge of a church.
explanation.walkthrough: Mark looks like part of the list of evangelists, but it is the definition, set off by and.
explanation.definitionFit: A notch is a small cut or nick made as a mark or tally.

clue.text: Who might share a kettle of hot water in Yorkshire Tea

blocks.note: H is the abbreviation for hot on taps
the Ouse is a Yorkshire river
maté is a South American herbal tea

explanation.surface: Putting the kettle on for a cup of the Yorkshire Tea brand.
explanation.walkthrough: Yorkshire Tea is a popular British tea brand; the clue splits it so Yorkshire goes with the river and Tea is maté.
explanation.definitionFit: A housemate lives in the same house, so shares the kitchen and its kettle.

clue.text: Ring style incorporating large creature but not small one

indicators.note: incorporating means taking into the body, so the style word wraps round the creature
but not excludes something, so the small creature is taken out of the large one

blocks.note: tone is a manner or style
an elephant is a large animal
an ant is a small creature

explanation.surface: A ring designed with a big animal but not a little one.
explanation.walkthrough: Ring is a verb meaning to call, not jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: To ring someone, in British usage, is to telephone them.

clue.text: Wrongly taking extraordinarily clear wisdom

indicators.note: extraordinarily means out of the ordinary way, so the letters are put in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
nous is common sense or wisdom

explanation.surface: Being mistaken while seeming remarkably wise.
explanation.definitionFit: Larceny is theft, so larcenous describes someone given to stealing what is not theirs.

clue.text: Entertainer using that in France to cover half of Just William?

indicators.note: using one thing in the word means bringing in a fresh part
to cover for someone is to stand in for them, so the French word takes the other part's place

blocks.note: a conjuror is a magician who entertains
que is French for that
the first half of the word just, which is what gets replaced

explanation.surface: A performer standing in for the boy hero of the Just William books.
explanation.walkthrough: Just William is a series of children's books about a scrape-prone schoolboy; only the William part defines, as William the Conqueror.
explanation.definitionFit: William I of England is known as William the Conqueror, so a conqueror is one William.

clue.text: Tendency of capital to stop etc in recession

indicators.note: stopping a gap plugs it, so the capital goes inside the other letters
recession is moving backwards, so the abbreviation is written in reverse

blocks.note: the abbreviation for et cetera written backwards
Lima is the capital of Peru

explanation.surface: An economist warning about money flows halting during a downturn.
explanation.walkthrough: Capital and recession suggest economics; capital is a city and recession a backward move.
explanation.definitionFit: The climate of opinion is its prevailing trend or tendency.

clue.text: Subtle nude dancing entertains party

indicators.note: dancing moves around, so the letters are rearranged
entertaining guests means having them in, so the rearranged letters hold the party

blocks.note: taken as written
the ANC, African National Congress, is a South African political party

explanation.surface: A tasteful naked dance performed at a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuanced means having fine shades of meaning, so it is subtle.

clue.text: More mature epitaph for US TV show?

blocks.note: RIP, rest in peace, is a standard epitaph
ER is an American hospital drama

explanation.surface: An older gravestone line for a cancelled American programme.
explanation.definitionFit: Riper is the comparative of ripe, which means fully developed or mature.

clue.text: Dish's invention

blocks.note: first meaning: a raised pastry filled with chopped pork
second meaning: a lie, in Cockney rhyming slang

explanation.walkthrough: The possessive makes it look like a recipe's creator; the two words are separate meanings. Rhyming slang turns lie into pork pie, often shortened to porky.
explanation.definitionFit: A pork pie is a classic British savoury pie, and in rhyming slang it means a lie, a made-up story.

clue.text: Red coat with light stole

blocks.note: rust is the red coating that forms on iron
an LED, light-emitting diode, is a light

explanation.surface: A scarlet jacket and a lamp went missing.
explanation.walkthrough: Stole looks like a shawl to go with the coat, but it is the past tense of steal.
explanation.definitionFit: To rustle is to steal livestock, so rustled means stole.

clue.text: Bread's inside that is empty

indicators.note: inside means placed within, so the bread goes into the abbreviation

blocks.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is
nan is a variant spelling of naan, an Indian flatbread

explanation.surface: The middle of the loaf has nothing in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Inane means silly or lacking sense, empty of meaning.

clue.text: He is cutting sign for reference

indicators.note: cutting into something goes inside it, so the first words sit within the sign

blocks.note: Taurus is a sign of the zodiac
he's is the short form of he is

explanation.surface: A man slicing through a signpost to point the way.
explanation.definitionFit: A thesaurus is a reference book listing words with similar meanings.

clue.text: Head of Tudor house standing by

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter
in a down entry, standing means upright, so the word is read from the bottom

blocks.note: the first letter of Tudor
a semi is a semi-detached house

explanation.surface: The owner of an old Tudor home waiting nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: A semi is a British house joined to one neighbour; by is the multiplication sign, as in three by four.
explanation.definitionFit: In arithmetic, by and times both mean multiplied by.

clue.text: An editorial department ultimately missing high-profile features?

indicators.note: ultimately missing means lacking at the end, so the final letter of the department goes

blocks.note: taken as written
a newspaper desk is an editorial department

explanation.surface: A newspaper section without its big feature articles.
explanation.walkthrough: Features suggests newspaper articles; here they are features of the landscape, and high-profile means tall.
explanation.definitionFit: The Andes are the South American mountain range, landscape features with a high profile.

clue.text: A strange calm curtailed icy hail

indicators.note: strange means odd or out of order, so these letters are rearranged
curtailed means having the tail cut off, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
icy without its last letter

explanation.surface: An oddly short, still spell of freezing weather.
explanation.walkthrough: Hail looks like frozen rain to match icy, but it is the verb meaning to praise.
explanation.definitionFit: To hail someone is to greet or praise them publicly, which is to acclaim them.

clue.text: Oscar sadly lied about father loving mother?

indicators.note: sadly suggests something gone wrong, so the letters of lied are jumbled
about means surrounding, so the jumbled letters go round the father

blocks.note: Oscar is O in the NATO alphabet
taken as written
pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: Oscar told a sad lie about his dad's love for his mum.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a loose definition: the Oedipus complex is a son's desire for his mother.
explanation.definitionFit: Oedipal describes a son's attraction to his mother, after the Greek king who unknowingly married his.

clue.text: Permanent resettlement of Leeds including north and south

indicators.note: resettlement moves things to new places, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the city name taken as written
N is the abbreviation for north
S is the abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: A lasting rehousing scheme for Leeds that takes in both ends of the country.
explanation.walkthrough: Leeds is a city in Yorkshire, northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Something endless goes on for ever, so it is permanent.

clue.text: Defer tariffs at last, with dollar overtaking pound

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word before it
overtaking here means taking over, so the currency surrounds the pound

blocks.note: the final letter of tariffs
USD is the currency code for the US dollar
a pound is an enclosure for animals, a pen

explanation.surface: Postponing import duties as the dollar overtakes sterling.
explanation.walkthrough: Pound looks like money next to dollar, but it is an animal enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: To suspend something is to put it off for a while, to postpone it.
